traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Euphorbiaceae (read 2026-10-17): blade given as undivided ('lamina entire', no dissected state listed); leaves mostly simple, compound ones palmate. Lobed blades (Ricinus, Manihot, Jatropha) exist but the page does not list them.

traits.flowering_position.note: DELTA Euphorbiaceae (read 2026-10-16): inflorescences terminal or axillary (Euphorbia and Croton often terminal, Acalypha and Macaranga axillary).

traits.perianth.note: Ranked by genus (pages read 2026-10-17). Euphorbia (~2,000 spp; naked flowers in the cyathium, per the Wikipedia Euphorbiaceae page the first pass read) counted as absent. Croton (1,100-1,300 spp; Wikipedia count, floral detail from the CoL Plantae/POWO-style genus account at colplanta.org: staminate flowers usually with 5 free petals, pistillate petals reduced or missing) counted as sepals_and_petals. Acalypha (~450-460 spp, Wikipedia: apetalous, small sepals only) counted as tepals. Macaranga (~300, Wikipedia) not counted: its page says nothing on the flowers. Counted tally: absent ~2,000, sepals_and_petals ~1,200, tepals ~450 (of ~3,650); absent leads by ~22% of counted species. Uncounted calyx-only genera (Macaranga, Mallotus, Tragia, Manihot) would narrow but probably not close the gap. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 259: merism mostly 4- or 5-merous, ranging from 3 to 8; Simpson p. 307 says generally 5-merous.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 309: Simpson's formula: ovary of 3 carpels, rarely 2 to many (Floral Diagrams p. 257 general formula: 3, rarely 1 or up to 20).

traits.ovary_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 309: gynoecium syncarpous with a superior ovary.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 505: Simpson calls the flowers hypogynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 133 Euphorbiaceae: herbs, shrubs or trees, some with milky sap; leaves alternate, rarely opposite, simple or compound, sometimes reduced, mostly with stipules; flowers unisexual, mostly both sexes on one plant; petals mostly absent; stamens from one to a thousand; ovary mostly of three cells; fruit a capsule or a drupe. Hutchinson's family also holds what APG sets apart as Phyllanthaceae and Picrodendraceae; only characters that hold for the narrower family are stated, and the perianth (sepals only in most, none in Euphorbia's cyathium) is left for a value the vocabulary has.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 309, 310, family Euphorbiaceae: inflorescence cyme, usually; read as {"cyme": "usually"}.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 309, 310, family Euphorbiaceae: flower symmetry actinomorphic, usually; read as {"actinomorphic": "usually"}. The books add zygomorphic (rarely): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 309, 310: zygomorphic.

traits.fruit_type.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add schizocarp (sometimes), berry (sometimes), samara (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 309, 310: schizocarp, drupe, berry or samara.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add whorled (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 309, 310: spiral, opposite or whorled.
